title: MKTG302: Email marketing
description:
About JerseySTEM

All JerseySTEM roles are pro-bono (unpaid) positions. JerseySTEM is a mission-driven professional network of pro-bono contributors dedicated to improving access to STEM education and career pathways for underserved middle school girls in New Jersey.
Members contribute their professional skills and leverage their networks in service of the organization’s gender-equity agenda.Membership is a minimum six-month commitment of approximately six flexible hours per week and includes a $100 refundable deposit, returned after six months of active membership. K-12 educators, retirees, veterans, interns, and students are exempt from the deposit.
Overview
This is a pro-bono volunteer position.
JerseySTEM is seeking an experienced Email Marketing Specialist to join our team. In this role, you will play a crucial part in our mission to provide STEM education to underserved middle school girls by effectively managing our email marketing campaigns. If you have a passion for both marketing and education, and you're ready to make a positive impact, we encourage you to apply.
Responsibilities

• Plan, execute, and optimize email marketing campaigns to engage our audience and drive desired actions.

• Develop captivating and relevant email content, including copywriting and design, to ensure messages resonate with recipients.

• Implement audience segmentation strategies to deliver personalized and targeted email campaigns.

• Conduct A/B tests on various email elements to refine content and increase campaign effectiveness.

• Utilize email marketing analytics tools to track and analyze campaign performance, making data-driven improvements.

• Oversee email list management, including maintenance, growth, and segmentation.

• Implement email marketing automation workflows to streamline processes and enhance engagement.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including content creators, designers, and developers, to execute email campaigns successfully.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, or a related field.

• Proven experience in managing email marketing campaigns and using email marketing platforms.

• Strong writing and copywriting skills with an understanding of email content optimization.

• Familiarity with email marketing analytics and reporting tools.

• Knowledge of email marketing best practices, including audience segmentation and A/B testing.

• Creative mindset and ability to create compelling email designs and layouts.

• Detail-oriented and organized with the ability to manage multiple email campaigns simultaneously.

title: Customer Support Specialist (Fintech & Crypto Payments)
description:
About the Client
We're helping a company in the fintech and digital assets industry find an experienced Customer Support Specialist to support users of its digital assets platform and associated crypto payment card.
The company operates within the evolving financial technology space, providing digital financial solutions that connect traditional payment services with cryptocurrency and digital assets.
As the business continues to grow, they're looking for their first dedicated Customer Support Specialist to take ownership of incoming customer inquiries, resolve issues, and help establish a reliable, high-quality customer support function.
The Role
We're looking for a Customer Support Specialist - Fintech & Crypto Payments who combines excellent customer service skills with a strong understanding of financial products, digital platforms, payment transactions, and ideally cryptocurrency.
You'll be the first point of contact for customers using the platform and its associated crypto card, helping them navigate account setup, verification, platform functionality, card usage, payments, deposits, withdrawals, and other transaction-related concerns.
The majority of support will be handled through live chat and written communication , with occasional phone or video calls when customers require more hands-on assistance.
As the first person joining this function, you'll be expected to take ownership of incoming cases and resolve issues independently wherever possible, following established SOPs and escalation procedures.
This is not a generic customer service role. We're looking for someone who can understand the product, investigate problems, identify solutions, and confidently guide customers through financial and technical issues.
Role Details
Commitment: Full-Time (40 hours/week)
Working Hours: Fixed Bahamas business hours (Eastern Time)
Location: Fully Remote
Engagement: Independent Contractor
Start Date: ASAP
Monthly Rate: US$1,200 - $1,600 (Depending on level of experience)
What You'll Do
Customer Support & Platform Assistance

• Serve as the primary point of contact for incoming customer inquiries through live chat, email, and other written channels.

• Handle phone or video calls when issues require more detailed or personalized assistance.

• Guide customers through account creation, onboarding, verification, and general platform navigation.

• Help customers understand and use the platform's features and services effectively.

• Investigate customer concerns, identify underlying issues, and provide accurate, timely resolutions.

• Take ownership of cases from initial contact through resolution, escalating only when necessary and in line with established SOPs.

• Maintain professional, clear, and reassuring communication throughout the customer journey.

Crypto Card & Payment Support

• Assist customers with crypto card issuance, activation, linking, and usage.

• Help customers understand transaction statuses, payment processes, and common reasons for unsuccessful transactions.

• Support customers with deposits, withdrawals, transfers, balances, and account-related transactions.

• Investigate transaction discrepancies and coordinate with internal teams where additional support is required.

• Provide clear guidance while maintaining accuracy when handling financial and transactional information.

Account Verification & Issue Resolution

• Guide customers through relevant KYC, identity verification, and account-related procedures.

• Troubleshoot common account access, verification, and platform issues.

• Independently investigate and resolve incoming cases using available tools, resources, and established procedures.

• Recognize when issues require escalation to operations, compliance, payments, or technical teams.

Nice to haves

title: Technical Program Manager, Life Sciences
locationText: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Scientists use Claude across the life sciences, from drug discovery and research biology to clinical development and manufacturing. To support that work, Anthropic introduced the Life Sciences Verification Program (LSVP), which gives verified life science professionals access to Claude with a refined set of safeguards that is more permissive for biology-related work. The program is in beta.We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to own the program of work that expands that access and helps scale it with safety in mind.

Each expansion depends on many teams at once and no single team owns the path end to end. You'll become the single owner of that program, the person who knows what each expansion requires, where every workstream stands, what it is waiting on, and who needs to decide. This is a cross-org execution role, not a research role, and it does not require a life sciences background. LSVP is the starting point, and the scope will grow alongside Anthropic's broader work in the life sciences. Over time, more of the life sciences community can get verified access, and each new expansion takes less bespoke effort than the last.

Responsibilities

• Own the program for expanding access to Anthropic's life sciences verification programs: scoping, sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs across safeguards, platform, and product engineering teams

• Scope and drive the cross-org engineering work that each expansion requires, from new plan and account types to new platforms

• Partner with the product manager to turn program goals into a sequenced plan with clear owners and dates

• Drive clarity on data access, retention, and review requirements, and on the changes they require across safeguards, access, and provisioning

• Drive user experience scoping across the Claude product surfaces where the program is available

• Find and remove the technical blockers that keep eligible organizations from accessing life sciences capabilities

• Establish the operating rhythm: a single view of workstreams, owners, dependencies, risks, and status, with planning, escalation paths, and launch coordination across orgs

• Convert recurring efforts into documented, repeatable processes so that each new expansion requires less bespoke coordination

You may be a good fit if you

• Have several years of experience in technical program management, with a track record of successfully delivering complex, cross-functional programs

• Have experience coordinating across multiple engineering teams and organizations simultaneously, including safeguards, platform, and product partners

• Can engage meaningfully with the engineers doing the work, from platform and access systems to product surfaces

• Are highly organized and can manage multiple parallel workstreams effectively across distributed teams

• Thrive in unstructured environments with a knack for bringing order to chaos and creating clarity in ambiguous situations

• Have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence without authority

• Have worked on cloud or platform programs (preferred but not required)

• Do not need a life sciences background. This is not a research role, and no life sciences experience is required

• Are passionate about Anthropic's mission and interested in the challenges of bringing AI capabilities to the life sciences community safely and reliably

title: Trustpilot SEO & Reputation Management Specialist (iGaming)

We are looking for a Trustpilot SEO & Reputation Management Specialist to join our partner teams and take responsibility for developing Trustpilot profiles of international iGaming brands. What you will do:

• Conduct SERP analysis for brand, brand reviews and other relevant keyword clusters.

• Create, verify, and optimize Trustpilot Business profiles.

• Work with names, descriptions, categories, contact details, images, promotional blocks, and other available profile elements.

title: Senior Platform Engineer
description:
Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning
 
Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive, feature-rich solution, empowering every team-from Finance to HR-to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.
 
Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally. Industry leaders like Unilever, Snowflake, Siemens, and DPD use Pigment daily to make more informed decisions and confidently navigate any scenario.
 
With a team of 600+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco and Austin, we've raised nearly $400M from top-tier investors and were named a Visionary in the 2024 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software.
 
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo-all while working as one team. If you're driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

The opportunity
 
We are looking for a Senior SRE profile who will design and implement the Pigment infrastructure for tomorrow. Pigment is a technically challenging platform. It calculates and synchronizes large datasets that must be updated in real-time. Data comes from client models that can be up to billions of rows. This data can be pivoted, transformed, and aggregated on-demand through our formula engine while rendering live on our front end.
Here are the challenges to be tackled as an SRE :
Define and build the infrastructure needed to answer our performance challenges, automate it, and make it scalable. In particular, ensure that the infrastructure scales in and out according to the platform usage.
Secure high availability and redundancy of the Pigment platform.
Ensure that the platform’s performance and correctness are monitored accordingly, spread observability best practices across the engineering team.
Participate in incident response.
Accompany Pigment geographical expansion as the company grows and we sign clients overseas.
Work with our security team on the implementation of their roadmap when related to infrastructure and development pipelines (code repository, credentials management, ...)
Continuously chase inefficiencies within our development practices and pipelines. Seek improvement and automation wherever possible. Drive change across the software engineering team.
In addition to SRE responsibilities, we expect you to contribute to software development activities. We believe SRE engineers should collaborate closely with software engineers, fostering a shared understanding of day-to-day challenges, rather than operating in separate teams. Last but not least, you will not be alone! You will be part of an SRE team.
 
Our Engineering team
Our Engineering team is responsible for developing our SaaS platform and building a comprehensive and user-friendly product.
Pigment engineers participate in the entire application development lifecycle, focusing on design, coding, and keeping the production platform up and running. They can be specialized, but there is no strict separation between the infrastructure, backend, and the frontend.
 
We value user-centricity and pragmatism: we choose the most relevant tools for the problem we have to solve, understanding the strengths and constraints of each technology.
Our engineering culture also values curiosity, humility, trust, ownership and team spirit.
 
Technical stack:
Kubernetes (GKE, hosted on Google Cloud Platform): hosting all our infrastructure components except some PostgreSQL hosts, hosted on Google Cloud SQL
Terraform: all our infrastructure is managed via this infrastructure as code (creation of GKE clusters, Google Cloud SQL databases, GCS buckets, IAM permissions...)
Databases: PostgreSQL (CloudSQL and CloudNativePG), SingleStore, ElasticSearch
RabbitMQ: queuing system
Temporal.io: workflow automation platform
Others: ArgoCD, Istio, Vault, Github, Do

title: GTM Data Quality Analyst
description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation - building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

THE OPPORTUNITY

You'll own the quality of the data that underpins every routing rule, territory, forecast and ARR number at CodeRabbit. You'll start by working the requests our GTM and Finance teams send to RevOps every day, and you'll turn each kind of request into a written runbook. Then you'll build the Data Quality Agent: an AI agent that handles most of those requests itself, routes the risky ones to a human for approval, and keeps a full record of everything it does. You'll join Business Systems, a small team that builds with agentic tools every day, and you'll work on the same engineering harness our engineers use to ship Salesforce and internal tool changes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own the tier-1 data queue for internal GTM systems data support: account ownership changes, account creation, merges, parent-child hierarchies, lead conversion, and linking billing subscriptions to the right Salesforce account.

- Resolve requests within the team's response standard and leave a record any teammate can pick up.

- Write and maintain a runbook for every recurring request type: the trigger, the checks, the steps, the edge cases, and when to escalate.

- Design, build and run the Data Quality Agent with Code Rabbit Coding Agent and our engineering harness, starting in shadow mode and earning its autonomy one workflow type at a time.

- Define the agent's approval tiers: what it can fix on its own, what it proposes for human approval, and what it always escalates.

- Run duplicate detection and merge cohorts across accounts, contacts and leads, and keep account hierarchies accurate as customers grow, merge and reorganize.

- Close enrichment gaps (firmographics, domains, HQ location, parent company) using our enrichment tools and the data warehouse.

- Track the request queue and data health with clear metrics: volume by request type, time to resolve, agent accuracy, and how often humans override the agent.

- Find the root cause behind repeat requests and bring proposals to the engineers so the fix lands upstream.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years in CRM data operations, sales operations, RevOps or data quality at a B2B SaaS company.

- Hands-on Salesforce experience: the Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity data model, ownership and sharing basics, reports, and bulk data tools.

- Strong SQL. You can answer your own questions from the warehouse without waiting on an analyst.

- You have used AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT to automate real work, and you can show us something you built: a prompt chain, a script, an agent, or an automation that saved hours.

- You write clear, step-by-step documentation that someone else can follow without asking you questions.

- Careful judgment with production data. You know which changes are easy to undo and which are not, and you treat them differently.

- Comfortable working across time zones with stakeholders in the US and Europe.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience with dedupe and merge tools such as Traction Complete, DemandTools, Cloudingo or Salesforce duplicate rules.

- Python or JavaScript scripting, Git, and comfort working in a code repository.

- Experience with enrichment and prospecting data tools such as Clay, Zoo

title: Medical Legal P&S Report Reviewer - Workers' Compensation
description:
We are seeking a detail-oriented Virtual Med-Legal P&S Report Reviewer to support a physician specializing in California Workers’ Compensation. In this role, you will be responsible for reviewing, quality-assuring, and editing Permanent & Stationary (P&S) and supplemental reports to ensure they are complete, internally consistent, accurately documented, and ready for final physician sign-off.
Key Responsibilities:
P&S & Supplemental Report QA (Primary):

• Verify demographics, claim details, dates of injury, and body parts across report sections.

• Cross-check injury history, objective exam findings, diagnoses, and narrative descriptions for internal consistency.

• Review supplemental reports to ensure they address new medical records, questions, or legal issues.

• Identify and flag missing, conflicting, or incomplete report sections prior to finalization.

• Proofread medical terminology, spelling, grammar, and ensure adherence to physician formatting templates.

WC Med-Legal Content Auditing:

• Review core components of P&S reports, including P&S/MMI status, mechanism of injury, accepted vs. disputed body parts, subjective/objective findings, diagnoses, WPI, apportionment, work restrictions, and future medical care.

• Ensure Whole Person Impairment (WPI) and apportionment entries are clearly documented and consistent.

Medical Records Review & Case Prep:

• Prepare case fact sheets prior to upcoming examinations.

• Compare report statements against supporting clinical records (dates, treatment history, diagnostics).

• Track and request missing medical records, maintain report templates/checklists, and document required corrections.

Requirements
Direct experience reviewing or editing Workers' Compensation med-legal reports (P&S, MMI, or impairment reports from any state).
Strong command of WC terminology, including P&S/MMI, WPI, apportionment, causation, work restrictions, and future medical care.
Working knowledge of the AMA Guides (5th Edition preferred).
Proven track record in clinical documentation review and medical records comparison.
Exceptional written English, medical proofreading skills, attention to detail, and independence.
Please note that this is a full-time contractor position (40 hours per week) with a starting pay rate of $6 per hour depending on skillset and experience. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am-5pm PST.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at a historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network.

In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea-and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own energy storage system design for a maritime autonomous vehicle. Reporting to the Vehicle Systems Lead, you will drive cell selection, module design, thermal management, and pressure-rated packaging for battery systems that must deliver ultra-long-range endurance under pressure.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own energy storage architecture: cell chemistry selection, module design, and pack integration

• Design pressure-rated battery enclosures for full-ocean-depth operation

• Perform battery sizing, energy budget analysis, and cycle life modeling

• Drive thermal management design for safe operation across environmental conditions

• Define charging profiles and integration with external charging interfaces

• Interface with energy distribution, structural, and production teams

• Support prototype builds, testing, and design-for-manufacturability reviews

• Contribute to safety analysis for energy storage systems

• Travel up to 25% to test sites and vendor facilities

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent

• 5+ years of experience in battery system design, energy storage, or power electronics

• Experience with lithium-ion or equivalent high-energy-density battery systems

• Familiarity with battery management systems and thermal management

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance

title: Director of Product, AI Labs
description:
About airSlate

airSlate is a global SaaS technology company that develops no-code workflow automation, electronic signature, and document management solutions. Our award-winning products - Sign Now, pdfFiller, DocHub, altaFlow, Instapage, and US Legal Forms - serve over hundreds of millions of users and more than one million customers worldwide, helping organizations of every size digitize processes, improve efficiency, and transform how they work.
We’re in an exciting phase of growth and transformation, with teammates in more than 20 countries across three continents and main hubs in the United States, Poland, Ukraine and Philippines .
At airSlate , we’re building value for customers and a culture where growth and innovation go hand in hand. We’re looking for people eager to shape products, scale a company, and thrive in a fast-moving environment.
Who we are

airSlate built a $1800M+ business serving dozens of millions of users across pdfFiller, SignNow, DocHub, AltaFlow and Instapage, on the back of a proprietary long-tail marketing engine. AI is now disrupting the core of that business and, at the same time, opening up a much bigger opportunity: solving the underlying business outcome end to end - draft, sign, track, invoice, collect - not just the document step.
The opportunity
We're running the company as two deliberately separate efforts. Our legacy portfolio - pdfFiller, DocHub, SignNow, AltaFlow - which we're optimizing for defensible 3-5 year revenue to fund what's next. AI Labs: a structurally separate, AI-native business we're building from scratch, targeting $20-50M of new topline in 2-3 years.
AI Labs is already proving the model works. BizDraft - AI-drafted agreements for SMBs - has shipped and is our learning vehicle for running a ~90% AI-driven product end to end. Ordinum, an AI compliance agent for regulated SMBs, is in development. BizPulse, which reconstructs a small business's financial and operational reality straight from its inbox, is in a controlled experiment. Alongside the products, AI Labs has rebuilt the pdfFiller editor from scratch (5x faster, 10x smaller) and stood up internal AI systems - Discovery Engine, document-based segmentation, Synthetic Users, Zero Reporting - that are starting to change how the rest of the company works.
We need a product leader to take AI Labs from "proving the model" to a real business.
The role
You'll own product for AI Labs: strategy, roadmap, and definition across our AI-native product line (BizDraft, Ordinum, BizPulse, and whatever comes next). You lead a small group of Product Owners, and will work in tight lockstep with AI Labs' engineering leadership, who own the build team.
A small go-to-market team - one product marketer and one marketer - supports AI Labs today, and you'll work closely with them on market analysis, idea generation, triage and prioritization, positioning, and launch.
What you'll do:

• Own product strategy and roadmap for AI Labs, targeting $20-50M in new AI-native topline over 2-3 years

• Scale BizDraft post-launch, drive Ordinum and BizPulse through to go/no-go for launch

• Identify, size and prioritize 2 to 5 more high-potential projects, based on established customer needs and a potential competitive advantage for airSlate

• Hire and lead a very small team of AI-native, 0-to-1 Product Owners, each owning the build out of a specific product against the prioritized ideas, and developing it based on customer and market feedback

• Develop a working understanding of our existing products (pdfFiller, SignNow, DocHub, AltaFlow) and their customers, to surface needs and use cases AI Labs can act on - some of which may be better rolled into an existing product as a feature rather than launched as a standalone AI Labs product

• Define product requirements and priorities with the precision AI-driven execution demands

• Partner closely with AI Labs' engineering lead on sequencing and trade-offs, without owning the engineering team directly

title: Field Marketer
description:
ABOUT CLIPBOARD

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/ and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

About the Role

As we have continued to expand, we want to meet the industry where it gathers. As a Field Marketer, you'll be Clipboard's face on the conference circuit in 2027. That means attending nearly every major Post Acute conference, trade show, and association event in the country. You'll work the floor, start conversations with agency owners and operators, qualify opportunities, and turn those conversations into pipeline and revenue.

This is a travel role. Expect to be on the road about 80% of the time. If living out of a suitcase sounds like a burden, this isn't the right role for you. If it sounds like an adventure and a big advantage in building a sales career, read on.

What You’ll Do

- Represent Clipboard in person at national, regional, and state conferences, trade shows, and industry events.

- Prospect aggressively before, during, and after every event: research attendee lists, book meetings ahead of time, and work the floor to start new conversations.

- Run discovery with Agency Owners, Administrators, Directors of Nursing, Clinical Managers, Directors of Operations, and staffing and recruiting leaders.

- Qualify opportunities and move them forward. Book next steps, convert interest into an active pipeline, and push deals toward close with the broader sales team.

- Work fluently across the organization within the sales team to ensure smooth handoffs after events.

- Share what you learn on the ground (customer pain points, competitor positioning, which events are worth our time) with sales, marketing, product and leadership.

Who You Are

- Willingness to travel about 80% of the time (roughly 40 weeks per year), including frequent overnight and multi-day trips.

- You must live in a major metro area within easy reach of a major airport.

- A valid driver's license and the ability to travel domestically without restriction.

- Comfortable working remotely and independently between events.

- Strong communication and relationship-building skills across clinical and business audiences.

- Curiosity, persistence, and a bias for action.

- Organization and autonomy in managing your own schedule and pipeline.

Our Interview Process

1. Case Study

2. Case Study Interview

3. Background Interview

4. Culture Interview (In Person)

5. Executive Chat

Because this role will primarily be in person at events, our culture round is held in person, and Clipboard covers all travel expenses. We want to see how you show up, and we want you to meet the team you'd be working with.

What We Offer

- Competitive base salary + uncapped commission

- Insurance benefits and 401k options

- Unlimited PTO and flexible holidays

- Mileage reimbursement or travel stipend for field work

- Remote flexibility when not in the field

- Clear growth path

Quick Note on Scammers:

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer Intern

ABOUT US

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like - and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds - which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia - many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact - this is the place.

About the role

Our Forward Deployed team works between our customers and our product. They take a customer’s whole support operation (the tickets, the systems, the policies) and turn it into AI agents that resolve real customer queries in production.

As an FDE intern, you’ll be part of that team from day one, not on a side project. The workflows you build will go live and handle real conversations for some of the largest fintech and healthtech companies in the US and Australia. You’ll have close support from the team and real ownership of the work you take on.

Day to day, you’ll:

- Dig into customers’ support tickets and data to find where AI can fully resolve queries, and where it can’t yet

- Build, test, and refine AI workflows from first draft through to production

- Help connect workflows to customer systems through APIs, and test integrations before they go live

- Join customer calls, share what you’ve found, and own defined parts of an implementation

- Use Claude Code and other AI tools to speed up analysis, build internal tooling, and improve how the team works

You’ll leave knowing how AI agents are deployed end to end at scale in regulated industries. You’ll also have hands-on skills in workflow design, API integrations, testing and evaluation, and LLM fundamentals, and experience turning a customer’s messy real-world problem into a working solution.

We’d love to talk if you

- Are curious and learn fast. You pick up new tools quickly and enjoy figuring things out.

A culture that's genuinely different. Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it - because life outside work matters. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.

A front-row seat to building something meaningful. We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company - not just execute someone else's vision.

Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar. Promotions happen when you're ready - leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.

title: Risk and Change Manager - Alpha Delivery PMO
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

- Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

- Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

- Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

- Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

You keep Alpha's cost and schedule baselines honest against each other. Without a credible risk register and change process, changes slip into the program outside any controlled path, the IMS and cost forecast quietly drift apart, and a gate review surprises leadership with numbers nobody signed off on. Your job is to prevent that by making risk and change management a live, trusted function from the earliest stage of delivery, rather than something bolted on once problems have compounded.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Establish and maintain the Alpha risk register across infrastructure, manufacturing and machine workstreams, facilitating structured risk identification, assessment and assignment of mitigation owners

- Own the change control process end to end, from intake and schedule, cost and technical impact assessment through to approval routing and the change log, working closely with the Cost Controller and Programme Schedule Manager so all baselines reflect the same accepted changes

- Prepare risk-adjusted inputs for release gate decisions, including quantified schedule and cost exposure and mitigation status

- Run regular risk reviews with workstream owners and escalate emerging risks early, before they reach senior leadership as surprises

- Build risk and change governance standards that scale as Alpha and Stellaris grow in parallel, with different partners and delivery models

- Support the PMO's wider reporting cadence alongside the PMO Analyst/Coordinator

WHO YOU ARE

- Experienced in risk and change management on major capital programs in energy, industrial, research infrastructure or similarly complex multi-discipline settings

- Able to build a risk and change framework from scratch, not just administer an inherited one; you know what good governance looks like before it exists

- Confident holding the line on change discipline with in

title: Director, Program Management
description:
Job Description Summary
As part of the GE Aerospace Digital Technology organization supporting the Defense & Systems (D&S) business, the Director, Program Management owns delivery across the Defense and Systems Customer Experience (DSCX) portfolio. This is a people-leadership role accountable for on-time delivery, program operating rhythms, dependency and risk management, and the scope, schedule, and cost tradeoffs for every program. This person will lead a team of program and project managers, set the delivery standard, and own the $25+MM CX budget in partnership with Finance and Business Operations. This person will be the single point of accountability for predictable execution and for escalating early when a dependency or decision threatens delivery. Job Description
Why This Role Exists
DSCX owns 30+ digital products for Defense & Systems. Today our technical product managers wear three hats for their products: product management, project management, and operations. We are dividing that load across three dedicated functions, and this role will build out the program management discipline, starting with on-time delivery across the portfolio. This role is planned to have 4-6 direct reports, program and project managers, and owns the $25+MM CX budget with Finance and Business Operations. Your charge is to build standard operating rhythms and artifacts, and then coach and train your team to hold them. You should be experienced with AI and know where it creates opportunity to expand what the team can deliver.

Environment
The DSCX portfolio runs primarily on AWS, Palantir Foundry, or through SaaS based 3rd party solutions, with on-premise implementations supported for customers whose data sensitivity requires it. Delivery runs through Rally and Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow is our system of record for incidents, change, and defect management. The portfolio carries a $25+MM annual budget across the product lines.

Roles and Responsibilities

Delivery

• Own on-time delivery (OTD) across the DSCX portfolio. OTD is the primary measure of this role. You set the target, run the cadence that surfaces risk against it, and close the gap.

• Run the operating rhythm so problems surface early. The weekly and monthly operating reviews (WOR and MOR), standups, reviews, and retros exist to make a slipping date visible weeks out, not on the date.

• Run Daily Visual Management across the portfolio. Delivery status and blockers are visible daily, which is what makes early escalation possible rather than aspirational.

• Make status honest and comparable. Every major program reports RAG status, milestones, and a path to green against one standard, so leadership compares programs instead of interpreting formats.

Dependency and Risk

• Keep programs from stalling on each other. You hold the dependency picture across DSCX and the partner teams we depend on, including Palantir, and resolve conflicts before they become schedule impacts.

• Drive risks to closure with a named owner and a date. The RAID log is the mechanism. Closure inside the committed date is the measure.

• Escalate early and with a recommendation. When a decision or dependency threatens a committed date, the sponsor hears it from you while there is still time to act, with the tradeoff already framed.

Scope, Schedule, and Cost

• Own the tradeoffs. Every program has a scope, schedule, and cost triangle. You either make the call or frame the decision for whoever should.

• Own the $25+MM CX budget with Finance and Business Operations, reconciled monthly, with committed versus actual accurate enough to plan against.

The next wave of enterprise software isn't about writing more code - it's about giving organizations the tools to combine trusted data, AI, and applications into systems that can reason and act on their own. Whether you're building this platform, proving its value to customers, or bringing it to market through our partner ecosystem, your work directly drives those outcomes for some of the most complex organizations in the world.
This is one of the most ambitious enterprise AI platforms in the market - built on decades of deep domain expertise across industries as varied as manufacturing, banking, insurance, financial services, and healthcare, and already running in production at real scale for organizations with some of the most demanding data and compliance requirements in the world. If you want to work at the intersection of enterprise AI, knowledge graphs, and agentic applications - with real customers and real production stakes, across nearly every major industry - this is where that work is happening.

ICX complements the systems customers already rely on, including PLM, ERP, MES, CRM and data platforms. It connects information across those systems, gives AI the context needed to reason, and enables people and agents to take measurable action through applications and orchestrated workflows.

title: Manager, Controls and Governance
description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me , Do the Right Thing , and Get Things Done . These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

This role focuses on strengthening OKX US' first line of defense while serving as the primary operational engine and bridge between the US business and control functions. Operating in a highly fluid environment, this position bridges the gap between hands-on internal controls and strategic US market execution.

You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with control functions across every aspect of the US business, from managing KYC/KYB onboarding pipelines and marketing content reviews to leading US executive reporting and customer support alignment. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, moves comfortably between granular risk management and growth strategy, and elevates organizational maturity to sustain OKX’s growth, integrity, and regulatory excellence.

 

 

What You’ll Be Doing

Controls Partnership & Operational Strategy

•
KYC / KYB Pipeline & Remediation: Support Compliance-managed KYC and KYB onboarding pipelines, identifying friction points, accelerating throughput between business units and Compliance, and resolving operational friction.

•
Risk Governance and Coordination: Serve as the key liaison to the US Risk organization, providing assistance in the monitoring of KRIs and the implementation of the risk framework.

•
Customer-Facing Content Governance: Lead the cross-functional workflow for Compliance and Legal reviews of growth assets, including marketing campaigns, product launches, promotional materials, and client communications.

•
Client Support & Compliance Alignment: Partner closely with Client Support and Compliance to streamline escalated customer workflows, ensure client support operations reflect regulatory requirements, and resolve customer-impacting compliance bottlenecks.

•
Controls Product Management: Work with Legal, Compliance, and Risk to understand key risks associated with new product launches, and utilize relationships with Product to promote innovation and product delivery.

 

Local Market Governance

•
Executive Reporting: Lead and coordinate reporting for executive meeting cadences, including soliciting updates and insight from business and control leads to present a cohesive view of US market performance and opportunities.

•
Policy & Procedures: Support the drafting and upkeep of operational policies and procedures. Prepare regular risk, control, and operational performance reporting for senior leadership.

•
First-Line Defense Leadership: Represent business operations in first-line risk management activities, supporting RCSAs, maintaining risk registers, and ensuring control effectiveness.

 

What We Look For In You

•
Experience: 3+ years of progressive experience in Strategic Operations, Program Management, Compliance Operations, Governance, or Risk Management within fintech, crypto/web3, or heavily regulated financial services.

•
Fluidity & Growth Mindset: A "builder" mindset with high comfort in ambiguous, rapidly evolving environments. Ability to pivot smoothly from tactical execution (tracking pipeline bottlenecks) to strategic alignment (launching new market initiatives).

•
Incident & Process Acumen: Proven track record leading cross-departmental incident response, mapping workflows, and executing post-incident

title: Senior Manager, Financial Crime Compliance, Suspicious Activity Reporting
description:

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.

 

About the role

Reporting to the FCC Transaction Monitoring Lead and sitting within the Financial Crime Compliance function, this role will lead and oversee a team of analysts and conduct independent, risk-based reviews of complex cases escalated from first- and second-line operations, covering KYC, name screening and transaction monitoring. The role will apply sound judgement and provide clear, well-supported outcomes in line with established procedures.

 

Responsibilities:

- Oversee, mentor and train a team of FCC L3 analysts, ensuring high-quality case resolution, adherence to SLAs and process governance.

- Review and resolve assigned KYC, enhanced due diligence, name-screening and transaction-monitoring cases, including alerts escalated from operational teams, in line with established procedures and applicable timelines.

- Assess customer profiles, ownership and control structures, business activities, transaction patterns, counterparties and relevant supporting information.

- Conduct appropriate internal and external research and critically assess information provided by customers or internal stakeholders.

- Reach clear, evidence-based conclusions or recommendations, documenting the rationale, supporting evidence and any required follow-up actions.

- Identify financial-crime risks, recurring themes and opportunities to improve processes or controls, and escalate complex or higher-risk cases, potential sanctions matches and suspicious activity concerns in line with established procedures.

- Apply relevant local and global Financial Crime Compliance policies and procedures, maintain complete and accurate case records, and collaborate effectively with Operations and Compliance stakeholders.

- Stay up-to-date with relevant financial-crime risks and regulatory developments, and support related Financial Crime Compliance Activities as needed.

- Perform any ad-hoc tasks required by the line manager.

 

What you will bring:

- Degree qualified or at least 8 years of working experience in the FCC space.

- Proven track record of working in an AML/CTF or fraud investigations role.

- Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to assess complex information and reach well-reasoned conclusions.

- Understanding of financial-crime risks, typologies and risk-based review practices.

- Sound judgement, ownership and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong attention to detail.

- Experience in FinTech or start-up experience is strongly preferred.
